claim.statement: The May 1-2 Teacher Day follow-up sample is dominated by loyalty and tribute rather than verified independent coordination: xPool emitted 68 items with about 36 loyalty/tribute-coded posts, repeated Keshvar-Doust 'country-loving teachers' invitations, and no clean source-near or social proof of an independent May 2 teacher strike or gathering.
claim.subject: Teacher Day public discourse

evidence.summary: The saved xPool dataset emitted 68 Persian items for teacher, livelihood, protest, and 12 Ordibehesht terms since 1 May.
Manual coding found loyalty/tribute content stronger than protest/repression content and no clean independent Teacher Day strike signal.
The existing SNN source announced the state-aligned Keshvar-Doust gathering for country-loving teachers.

information_depth.rationale: The sample is useful for discourse and negative evidence, but xPool is not representative and cannot prove offline absence.

assessment.uncertainty: Independent teacher-council or local action reports after May 2 could change the read.

claim.statement: Teacher Day ceremony is coexisting with a continuing teacher-repression lane: the ledger already records Kerman teacher activists facing six-month prison terms and 70-million-toman fines, and the v25 xPool sample surfaced a Kurdistan Human Rights Network report that Alan Hekmati-Rad, an English teacher from Mahabad detained on 18 Farvardin 1405, was in Naqadeh prison under temporary detention.
claim.subject: teacher activists and teachers
claim.object: prison, fines, and temporary detention alongside Teacher Day ceremony

evidence.summary: Sedaye Mardom reported prison enforcement and 70-million-toman fines against named Kerman teacher activists.
The xPool sample includes a Kurdistan Human Rights Network post naming Alan Hekmati-Rad and saying he was held in Naqadeh prison under temporary detention.
The source notes mark the Alan Hekmati-Rad item as useful texture requiring direct-article follow-up.

information_depth.rationale: The Kerman case has named details from an activist/media source already in the ledger; the Mahabad case is a credible rights-network social item but lacks a captured direct article in this pass.

assessment.uncertainty: Find direct KHRN article or court/family confirmation before treating the Alan Hekmati-Rad detention as fully verified.

claim.statement: On 1 May 2026, Persian parliamentary and retiree-facing reporting kept teacher and retiree pay grievances alive: a Babol MP asked why 1401 retired teachers' ranking decrees had not been corrected or issued and why end-service bonuses remained unpaid, EghtesadOnline carried criticism that retiree pension decrees had lost transparent salary line items, and ILNA/Vista quoted a Babol MP warning the 1405 budget was inflationary and insufficient for fixed-salary employees and retirees.
claim.subject: retired teachers and fixed-salary retirees
claim.object: ranking, pension-transparency, bonus, and inflation grievances

evidence.summary: Roozno/Vista reported the Babol MP's questions about uncorrected 1401 retired-teacher ranking decrees, unpaid end-service bonuses, and absorption of experienced education workers.
EghtesadOnline reported retiree criticism that pension decrees had deleted salary line items and created opacity, including education-retiree concerns over shortfalls.
ILNA/Vista quoted a Babol MP warning that the 1405 budget was inflationary and insufficient for employees and retirees whose fixed wages lag inflation.

information_depth.rationale: The claim rests on multiple Persian domestic reports with named parliamentary or retiree representatives and concrete mechanisms.

claim.statement: Education Ministry-linked reporting shows the sector being managed through damage repair and pay claims at the same time: the minister said roughly 1,300 schools or educational units were damaged in the recent war, 20 were fully destroyed, 775 lightly damaged schools had been returned to the education cycle, and more than 60 hemats of retirement bonuses had been paid while teacher decrees were issued quickly.
claim.subject: Iranian education sector
claim.object: school repair claims and teacher-payment claims

evidence.summary: Eghtesad Gostar quoted the minister on about 1,300 damaged schools/units, 20 fully destroyed, 775 lightly damaged schools rebuilt, rebuild timing, and more than 60 hemats of retirement bonuses.

information_depth.rationale: The figures are concrete but are ministry claims relayed through a Persian outlet; independent school-damage or payment audits are absent.

assessment.uncertainty: The damage and payment figures should be cross-checked against direct ministry releases or provincial education reports.

claim.statement: The v25 xPool Teacher Day sample shows pay grievance persisting inside the loyalty frame: among 67 string tweet texts, about 30 contained pay/livelihood language, including repeated references to teachers' meager pay and comments asking that teachers' and workers' salaries be increased or funded.
claim.subject: v25 xPool Teacher Day sample
claim.object: pay grievance embedded in tribute and loyalty discourse

evidence.summary: The saved dataset contains the Teacher Day social sample used for the count.
Manual and keyword coding found roughly 30 pay/livelihood texts and notes representative phrases about meager pay and salary increases.

information_depth.rationale: The count is bounded to the saved xPool sample and is useful for texture, not population measurement.

synthesis.title: Cracks in the Islamic Republic, v25 - Teacher Day split screen
synthesis.summary: Teacher Day follow-up currently resolves toward managed ceremony, not independent coordination. The visible public lane is crowded with loyalty/tribute material: `#سپاس_معلم`, Keshvar-Doust 'country-loving teachers' invitations, remembrance of the martyred leader, allegiance language, and even field-class mobilization before nightly gatherings. The v25 xPool sample emitted 68 items and showed far more loyalty/tribute than protest or named repression, with no clean evidence of a May 2 independent teacher strike. But the managed frame is brittle because the same window carries unresolved teacher and retiree pay questions, 1401 retired-teacher ranking decrees and end-service bonuses, nontransparent pension decrees, budget/inflation pressure on fixed-salary groups, school war-damage repair claims, and continuing coercion against teacher activists. Net: the regime can still choreograph Teacher Day in public, but it is choreographing over a professional base squeezed by pay, pension, infrastructure, and repression pressures.
synthesis.limitations: This pass is strong for public Teacher Day framing, pay-grievance persistence, and the absence of a clean independent coordination signal in the searched sample. It is weaker for offline attendance and local school-level action: xPool is not representative, Kerman repression remains activist/media-sourced, and the Alan Hekmati-Rad detention signal needs a direct article or court/family confirmation. Follow May 3-7 for teacher-council statements, repeat retiree/teacher gatherings, and whether the Keshvar-Doust event produces counter-mobilization.

information_depth.rationale: The synthesis combines bounded social sampling, domestic Persian reporting, existing Kerman/SNN rows, and explicit limitations around offline coordination.

operations.rationale: The Teacher Day follow-up sample resolves the immediate ceremony-window question toward managed/loyal channels rather than independent coordination.
Teacher repression beneath Teacher Day ceremony shows that livelihood and professional grievances still have a coercive/security boundary.
Retired-teacher ranking, pension, and bonus grievances keep the teacher/retiree labor-pressure lane active even without national coordination evidence.
The social sample shows livelihood language persisting even where Teacher Day is framed through tribute and loyalty.
